authoritative_for: Nucleus owns version-one invocation admission, one supervised attempt per job, job and cancellation lifecycle, exact harness-output atoms, immutable schema and toolset registrations, the durable requester-tool mailbox, and its credential lease.

Nucleus SQLite is authoritative for its operational job, attempt, registration, cancellation, mailbox, and output records; the installed service owns its per-user socket, private Codex home, and service lifecycle.
not_authoritative_for: Each requester remains authoritative for the domain state, domain success, idempotent mutation, duplicate handling, and whether a new attempt is safe.
Codex owns harness and account behavior, and Nucleus output or terminal state does not make model prose, a tool result, or a requester outcome domain truth.

covers: All supported public Nucleus version-one CLI and HTTP execution and service outcomes, requester-integration operations, and Nucleus development operations in this release.
excludes: Help and version display, implementation primitives, requester-owned workflows and domain operations, direct SQLite access, unsupported harnesses, current live readiness, and Codex behavior outside the proved adapter contract are outside this inventory claim.

shared_access_and_trust: The standard runtime is a current-user local service over a filesystem-protected Unix socket with no application-level authentication or TCP listener.
Installed discovery grants no socket, credential, workspace, tool, service-control, or retry authority; each entry declares its narrower invocation and effect boundary.
shared_privacy_and_retention: Nucleus private state may contain complete prompts, tool arguments and results, source content, exact harness output, terminal diagnostics, and authentication material.
Nucleus promises no automatic pruning policy for retained job or output records; provider documentation must contain no credentials, private runtime records, or requester source bodies.
compatibility_and_retirement: Provider release, entry contract version, public invocation protocol, store schema, adapter version, exact harness compatibility, and immutable schema or toolset identity are separate compatibility axes.
Incompatible public meanings require a new version and retained historical decoding; no broader compatibility window or deprecation period is promised unless an entry states one.
operational_limits: Version one admits exactly one attempt per job and provides no automatic retry, workflow graph, project registry, capability directory, requester-domain interpretation, or global drain command.
Live acceptance remains bounded by installed service, credential, adapter, account, local storage, and exact harness readiness, none of which provider installation proves.
